newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS Holding wraps up Elektrowatt withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: CS Holding wraps up Elektrowatt withdrawal.

text.p: Swiss financial company CS Holding Monday wrapped up its long-intended withdrawal from the industrial sector by selling a large part of its Elektrowatt AG electronics company to German electronics giant Siemens AG as part of a deal totalling more than 2 billion Swiss francs ($1.49 billion).
The sale followed last week's deal in which CS Holding agreed to sell the energy-related portions of Elektrowatt to a Swiss-German consortium.

"In concentrating on our core business, we have sought a new shareholder structure for Elektrowatt. We are delighted that viable and promising solutions have been found for both the energy and industry segments," CS Holding Chairman Rainer Gut said in a statement.

The sale of most of CS Holding's 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt, one of the world's leading building control and security system companies will produce a profit on paper of about 1 billion Swiss francs ($745 million).

The profit will directly offset charges of a similar amount that CS Holding took in July to cover the costs of a major corporate restructuring, including changing the name to Credit Suisse Group and cutting some 5,000 jobs worldwide, a spokesman said.

The gain from the sale will not change CS Holding's forecast for this year for a net loss of 2.1 billion francs ($1.6 billion) due to charges of 3.9 billion francs ($2.9 billion) in connection with a change in the method for calculating credit risks.
Excluding these charges, CS Holding's net profit in 1996 would have risen some 17 percent to 1.8 billion francs ($1.3 billion).
CS Holding's divestment of its stake in Elektrowatt has been a lengthy process that required many steps.

The process began in November when Elektrowatt announced it would spin off its power and electricity activities into a separate company, Watt AG. CS Holding would retain a 44.9 percent stake in Watt and in the remaining Elektrowatt.
Elektrowatt's shareholders are scheduled to vote on the split of the company in February.

Last week, CS Holding sold off around 30 percent of its shares in Watt for around 1 billion francs ($745 million) to a consortium comprising German energy companies Bayernwerk, Badenwerk and Energieversorgung Schwaben (EVS) and Swiss utility Nordostschweizerische Kraftwerke (NOK).
The sale to Siemens of its 44.9 percent stake in the industrial activities of Elektrowatt completes the process.
Following the expected spin-off of Watt in February, Siemens will take over CS Holding's shares in Elektrowatt for 285 francs ($212) a share, or around 1.1 billion francs ($821 million).
Siemens will then make a public offer to other Elektrowatt shareholders at the same price.
